subject.title: [Feature]: Opt-in allowlist (hydrateEnv/passEnv) for which env vars reach spawned child processes (exec + app-server)

question: Should OpenClaw add a canonical opt-in child-process environment policy, and what precedence should it have over existing exec sanitization, Codex `clearEnv`, and upstream Codex `shell_environment_policy`?
rationale: This changes a credential boundary and adds compatibility-sensitive configuration across multiple runtimes; source inspection can establish the exposure but cannot choose the intended default or ownership model safely.

options.title: Add opt-in canonical policy
options.body: Introduce a backward-compatible policy with explicit inheritance and positive selection, then apply it consistently at verified OpenClaw-owned spawn boundaries.

options.title: Adopt default-deny
options.body: Make new and upgraded installations pass only a minimal environment, with doctor migration and extensive compatibility proof for existing deployments.

options.title: Keep existing controls
options.body: Retain targeted exec sanitization and `appServer.clearEnv`, documenting upstream Codex configuration as the narrower app-server workaround.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in canonical policy
recommendation.body: Introduce a backward-compatible policy with explicit inheritance and positive selection, then apply it consistently at verified OpenClaw-owned spawn boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available history-based routing candidate on the adjacent host-exec policy surface, though ownership of the cross-runtime configuration decision remains uncertain.
